entities.name: relevant test component, timer or port

requirements.subject: ent:test-behaviour
requirements.canonical: Test behaviour CAN be expressed sequentially, as a set of alternatives, or as a combination of both.
requirements.original: Test behaviour cannot only be expressed sequentially, but also as a set of alternatives or combinations of both.

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: The `interleave` statement CAN specify interleaved sequences or alternatives.
requirements.original: An interleaving operator allows the specification of interleaved sequences or alternatives.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 20 and table 19 call the construct the interleave statement; 'interleaving operator' is used only here.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: Alternative behaviour IS expressed with the `alt` statement, written `alt { … }`.
requirements.original: Alternative behaviour; Col2: alt { … }

requirements.subject: ent:repeat-statement
requirements.canonical: Re-evaluation of an `alt` statement IS expressed with the `repeat` statement, written `repeat`.
requirements.original: Re-evaluation of alt statements; Col2: repeat

requirements.subject: ent:interleave-statement
requirements.canonical: Interleaved behaviour IS expressed with the `interleave` statement, written `interleave { … }`.
requirements.original: Interleaved behaviour; Col2: interleave { … }

requirements.subject: ent:activate-operation
requirements.canonical: A default IS activated with the `activate` operation, using the keyword `activate`.
requirements.original: Activate a default; Col2: activate

requirements.subject: ent:deactivate-operation
requirements.canonical: A default IS deactivated with the `deactivate` operation, using the keyword `deactivate`.
requirements.original: Deactivate a default; Col2: deactivate

requirements.subject: ent:alternative-behaviour
requirements.canonical: Sequences of statements CAN be expressed as sets of possible alternatives that form a tree of execution paths.
requirements.original: A more complex form of behaviour is where sequences of statements are expressed as sets of possible alternatives to form a tree of execution paths, as illustrated in figure 9.

requirements.subject: ent:alt-statement
requirements.canonical: The `alt` statement IS the statement that expresses sequences of statements as sets of possible alternatives forming a tree of execution paths.
requirements.original: This is done with the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: When an `alt` statement is entered, a snapshot IS taken.
requirements.original: When entering an alt statement, a snapshot is taken.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS a partial state of a test component.
requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean guards of the alternative branches.
requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including all relevant stopped test components.
requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including all relevant timeout events.
requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS including the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.
requirements.original: A snapshot is considered to be a partial state of a test component that includes all information necessary to evaluate the Boolean conditions that guard alternative branches, all relevant stopped test components, all relevant timeout events and the top messages, calls, replies and exceptions in the relevant incoming port queues.

requirements.subject: ent:relevant-entity
requirements.canonical: A test component, timer or port that is referenced in at least one alternative of the `alt` statement IS relevant for the snapshot.
requirements.original: Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.

requirements.subject: ent:relevant-entity
requirements.canonical: A test component, timer or port that is referenced in a top alternative of an altstep invoked as an alternative in the `alt` statement IS relevant for the snapshot.
requirements.original: Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.

requirements.subject: ent:relevant-entity
requirements.canonical: A test component, timer or port that is referenced in a top alternative of an altstep activated as a default IS relevant for the snapshot.
requirements.original: Any test component, timer and port which is referenced in at least one alternative in the alt statement, or in a top alternative of an altstep that is invoked as an alternative in the alt statement or activated as default is considered to be relevant.

readings: A test component, timer or port referenced in a top alternative of any altstep that is currently activated as a default IS relevant for the snapshot.
A test component, timer or port referenced in a top alternative of an altstep activated as a default within the alt statement IS relevant for the snapshot.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of 'activated as default' is unclear (activated anywhere vs. within the alt statement); chose the first reading, because defaults are activated outside the alt statement and are appended to every alt.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: A snapshot IS only a conceptual means for describing the behaviour of the `alt` statement.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Snapshots are only a conceptual means for describing the behaviour of the alt statement.

requirements.subject: ent:snapshot
requirements.canonical: Taking a snapshot IS instantaneous (has no duration) in the TTCN-3 semantics.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The TTCN-3 semantics assumes that taking a snapshot is instantaneous, i.e. has no duration.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: In a real implementation, taking a snapshot CAN take some time and race conditions CAN occur.
requirements.original: In a real implementation, taking a snapshot may take some time and race conditions may occur.

requirements.subject: ent:race-condition
requirements.canonical: The handling of race conditions caused by non-instantaneous snapshots IS NOT within the scope of the present document.
requirements.original: The handling of such race conditions is outside the scope of the present document.
